articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rheum australe is an important medicinal herb known as Himalayan rhubarb. Traditionally used in Ayurveda and Tibetan medicine to treat diabetes, diarrhoea, hypertension, obesity, wounds, backache & gastrointestinal diseases. AIM OF THE STUDY: The current study is focused on studying the antibacterial and synergistic potential of the anthraquinone-enriched fraction of R. australe in combination with conventional antibiotics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The extract of R. australe was prepared using 70% ethanol with a Soxhlet apparatus, and Bioassay guided fractionation was done. Broth microdilution methods determined antibacterial and Synergistic activity of crude extracts and subfractions. Phytoconstituents were identified by LC-MS, and molecular docking was done to study the interaction with penicillin-binding protein 3, and docking-predicted potential interacting Phytoconstituents were quantified by HPLC. RESULTS: The extraction yield of the hydroalcoholic extract was recorded as 40.66 ± 3.05%. The chloroform subfraction showed the strongest antibacterial activity among all the subfractions against MRSA (64 μg/ mL), S. aureus (16 μg/mL) &P. aeruginosa (8 μg/mL) mL, and also the strongest synergistic activity with tetracycline against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (FICI 0.19-0.5), Staphylococcus aureus (FICI 0.0312-0.125), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (FICI 0.125-0.375). Six phytoconstituents (piceatannol, chrysophanol, rhein, aloe-emodin, physcion & emodin) were identified by LC-MS. Molecular docking and MD simulation data revealed that among all the phytoconstituents, aloe-emodin, chrysophanol, emodin, & rhein indicated favourable interactions. HPLC analysis showed that these four phytoconstituents were enriched in the chloroform subfraction. CONCLUSION: The current study suggests that the chloroform subfraction enriched in anthraquinones exhibits strong antibacterial activity and synergistic activity in combination with tetracycline, and the synergistic mechanism of the combination remains to be established.

articles.title: Inhibitory action of Origanum onites essential oil on scorpion venom induced smooth muscle contractions.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Androctonus crassicauda and Mesobuthus gibbosus are scorpions with powerful toxins with causes of envenomations leading to death but they are also potential candidates for drug development. Pharmacological investigations on venoms of Androctonus crassicauda (Acr) and Mesobuthus gibbosus (Mgb) are few. Ethnopharmacological use of Origanum species against envenomations was noted by Dioscorides. AIM OF THE STUDY: Aim of the study was to investigate actions of Acr and Mgb on prostatic and epididymal segments of isolated rat vas deferens and to investigate effects of Origanum onites essential oil (OOeo) against actions of these venoms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Acr and Mgb were tested on phenylephrine- CaCl2- and KCl-induced contractions of prostatic and epididymal segments of isolated rat vas deferens. Effects of OOeo on actions of venoms were tested. Regular expressions were used for short linear motifs and Clustal omega for multiple sequence alignment of toxins and TRPA1. RESULTS: Both venoms inhibited phenylephrine-induced contractions but augmented KCl-induced contractions. CaCl2-induced contractions were not affected. Parallel shift of dose-response curve of Mgb was found. Molecular mimicry using GxxxG (GG4) motif that has the structure [GS]xx[FY]GYC was found indicating role of TRPA1 ion channels. This motif was evolutionary conserved from Cnidaria to mammals. Dose-dependent inhibitory actions of OOeo against Acr-induced contractions of epididymal vas deferens indicated possible roles of TRPA1 and voltage-dependent Na+-channels. CONCLUSION: Contractile actions of the venoms on vas deferens and dose dependent inhibitory actions of OOeo against these venoms supply pharmacological evidence for the ethnopharmacological use of OOeo.

articles.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Differential Mechanisms of Four TCM Formulations in Treating Insomnia via Syndrome-Compound-Metabolite Association Networks.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Guipi Pills (GPW), Wuling Capsule (WLC), Bailemian Capsule (BLMC), and Zaoren Anshen Capsule (ZRASC) are representative traditional Chinese medicine formulations for treating insomnia based on different syndromes of Heart-Spleen Deficiency, Heart-Kidney Disharmony, Liver Qi Stagnation with Yin Deficiency, and Heart Blood Deficiency, respectively. However, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To elucidate the "same disease, different treatment" mechanisms of these four formulations against sleep deprivation-induced insomnia through an integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Chemical constituents were characterized by UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS. A meta-analysis evaluated clinical differences and syndrome consistency. Subsequently, A mouse model of sleep deprivation was established; behavioral tests and HE/Nissl staining were performed. On this basis, fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, serum metabolomics, and hypothalamic transcriptomics were integrated to construct a microbiota-metabolite network. Furthermore, network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted component-target interactions. Finally, key protein expression was validated by western blot. RESULTS: UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 87, 56, 163, and 128 compounds from GPW, WLC, BLMC, and ZRASC, respectively. Meta-analysis (62 RCTs, 6,045 patients) showed WLC and BLMC reduced PSQI scores alone or in combination; ZRASC benefited only in combination, and GPW combination benefit was borderline. Syndrome-efficacy interactions were inconsistent. In mice, all formulations alleviated neuronal damage despite heterogeneous behavioral improvements. All four formulations suppressed Alistipes and commonly reversed 39 serum metabolites enriched in glutathione metabolism and pentose phosphate pathway. Each formulation showed syndrome-related metabolic regulation. Hypothalamic transcriptomics revealed commonly downregulated genes (S100a9, Gbp5, Fpr1, Tnfsf8) and distinct patterns: lipid metabolism-immune suppression (GPW), transcriptional-metabolic inhibition (WLC), prolactin signaling (BLMC), and PPAR-driven energy repair (ZRASC). In an exploratory analysis, the number of microbiota-metabolite association pairs increased from WLC (158) to GPW (393), BLMC (836), and ZRASC (1,243); this gradient is hypothesis-generating and warrants independent validation.Network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted potential formulation-specific and common inflammatory pathway targets. Finally, western blot showed all formulations downregulated iNOS and COX2; all except WLC upregulated SLC7A11, GPX4, FTH, and Bcl2 (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: In this study, these four formulations showed heterogeneous, syndrome-associated patterns across microbiota remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, anti-inflammation, and anti-ferroptosis, which may help generate hypotheses regarding the "same disease, different treatment" principle. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for clinical application and a methodological reference for TCM modernization.

articles.title: Heifan Sanwei Decoction accelerates mucosal healing of acetic acid-induced oral ulceration: Potential involvement of C3/C5/C5aR1 signaling and macrophage phenotypic modulation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Heifan Sanwei Decoction (HFSWD) is a classic topical Mongolian and Tibetan medicinal formula within the system of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). It was first documented in Tongwa Gajid, a classic work of Tibetan medicine, and has subsequently been included in the second batch of the Catalogue of Ancient Classic Formulas. HFSWD consists of Melanterite (FeSO4·7H2O), Terminalia chebula Retz. and Eriobotrya japonica (Thunb.) Lindl.. Traditionally, it is used for ulcerative disorders of the tongue, oral cavity, and gingiva. In contemporary clinical practice, HFSWD is applied to oral inflammatory conditions, particularly recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), characterized by ulcerative and erosive mucosal lesions. However, the pharmacological mechanisms and bioactive constituents underlying its mucosal healing effects remain largely unexplored. AIM OF STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the mucosal healing-promoting effects of HFSWD in a rat model of acetic acid-induced oral ulceration and to explore the underlying mechanisms and bioactive constituents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Oral ulcers were induced in rats by acetic acid cauterization. Following topical HFSWD treatment, ulcer area and body weight were monitored over a 9-day period. Histological repair was assessed using H&E, Masson's trichrome, and immunofluorescence staining. In vitro wound healing, tube formation, and qRT-PCR assays were conducted to validate the pro-migratory and anti-inflammatory properties of HFSWD. Proteomic profiling and Western blotting were employed to explore the underlying mechanisms. Chemical component analysis, molecular docking and molecular dynamic (MD) simulations were further applied to explore candidate bioactive constituents and their potential interactions with relevant molecular targets. RESULTS: HFSWD treatment markedly reduced the ulcer area and effectively accelerated the overall wound-healing process in this model. Histological analysis revealed that HFSWD attenuated the local inflammatory response, promoted epithelial regeneration and collagen deposition, and significantly upregulated CD31 and CD206 expression while downregulating CD86. In vitro, HFSWD facilitated L929 and HOMF cell migration, enhanced angiogenesis in HUVECs, and suppressed the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 in LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages. Integrated proteomic and Western blot analyses further demonstrated that HFSWD markedly downregulated the elevated levels of C3, C5 and C5aR1 in vivo, whereas it reduced iNOS and C5aR1 and upregulated Arg-1 in LPS-stimulated macrophages. In silico predictions speculated chebulinic acid and chlorogenic acid as compounds with favorable theoretical binding affinities to the target proteins C3 and C5aR1, respectively. CONCLUSION: HFSWD accelerated mucosal healing in rats with acetic acid-induced oral ulcers, accompanied by attenuated local inflammation, promoted tissue repair, and modulated macrophage-related responses. These beneficial effects may be mediated by the suppression of complement-related inflammatory signaling involving C3, C5, and C5aR1, as well as alterations in macrophage polarization-associated markers.

articles.title: Probenecid promotes relaxation and potentiates the effects of cyclic nucleotide-elevating agents in the pig detrusor.
articles.abstract: Probenecid is a uricosuric agent also used as an antibiotic adjuvant. It inhibits, organic acid transporters (OATs), multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs) and pannexin-1 (Panx-1) channels and activates transient receptor potential vanilloid 2. We hypothesized that probenecid could modulate detrusor smooth muscle reactivity, either alone or in combination with relaxant agents. Functional, biochemical, and immunohistochemical approaches were employed. The relaxant effects of probenecid (1 nM-1 mM) were assessed in isolated pig detrusor alone and in combination with inhibitors or antagonists. The effects of probenecid preincubation (0.1, 0.3, and 1 mM) on relaxations induced by cAMP- or cGMP-elevating agents were also evaluated. Probenecid produced concentration-dependent relaxation with a maximal response of 56% and potentiated the relaxations induced by salbutamol, forskolin, riociguat, cilostazol, and tadalafil. Potentiation of salbutamol- and tadalafil-induced relaxations was prevented by the soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC) inhibitor, ODQ. In detrusor stimulated with sGC modulators, probenecid increased intracellular and reduced extracellular cGMP levels, whereas the cAMP levels were unaffected. Selective pharmacological tools targeting OAT, P2X7, and Panx-1 did not reproduce the potentiating effects of probenecid. Immunofluorescence revealed PDE3A, PDE5, and MRP4 expression in the urothelium, lamina propria, and smooth muscle, with the highest intensity in the urothelium. In conclusion, probenecid potentiates detrusor relaxation, an effect associated with an increased intracellular-to-extracellular cGMP ratio. These findings support further investigation of probenecid, alone or combined with clinically approved agents such as tadalafil or cilostazol, as a potential therapeutic approach for overactive bladder dysfunction.

articles.title: Motor patterns and neuromuscular transmission in different colonic segments of patients with Hirschsprung's disease studied ex vivo.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hirschsprung's disease is a congenital disorder characterized by the absence of ganglion cells in the distal bowel, leading to functional obstruction. This study aimed to assess the myogenic motor patterns and neuromuscular transmission in ex vivo colonic segments-ganglionic, transitional, and aganglionic-obtained from pediatric patients with Hirschsprung's disease. METHODS: Colonic segments from 7 patients were collected during surgery and colonic strips were studied in vitro. Myogenic activity, as well as inhibitory and excitatory neuromuscular responses, were evaluated using isometric force transducers and microelectrodes. RESULTS: All segments exhibited spontaneous myogenic slow phasic contractions. Inhibitory neuromuscular transmission, characterized by inhibitory junction potentials or muscle relaxation induced by electrical field stimulation (EFS)-, was robust in ganglionic segments, reduced in transitional zones, and largely absent in aganglionic segments. Despite this, aganglionic tissue responded to nitric oxide donors and partially to purinergic agonists, indicating the presence of post-junctional relaxation mechanisms. Excitatory transmission was preserved in ganglionic segments and mediated via cholinergic pathways, as confirmed by atropine sensitivity. The response was reduced in transitional zones, and aganglionic segments lacked functional excitatory responses to EFS but responded to direct muscarinic agonists. Acetylcholinesterase inhibition enhanced contractions, suggesting the presence of excitatory nerves. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides functional evidence correlating neuromuscular activity with histopathological findings in Hirschsprung's disease . While neural-mediated responses are absent in aganglionic zones, muscle and receptor-level responses are partially preserved, highlighting potential pharmacological targets, such as nitric oxide donors or antimuscarinic agents, for managing colonic motility in Hirschsprung's disease.

articles.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Orchestrate Diabetic Podocytopathy Through ROS/NLRP3/Pyroptotic Axis and Gut-Kidney Microbiota Crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Emerging evidence indicates that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute significantly to podocyte injury in DN:however, the specific underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study demonstrates that NET biomarkers are elevated in diabetic mice and patients with diabetes and positively correlate with DN severity. Treatment with deoxyribonuclease Ⅰ (DNase I), which degrades NETs, partially prevented podocyte dysfunction and renal injury. Mechanistically, NET formation triggered excessive generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), activating the nuclear factor-κB ( NF-κB) signaling pathway and NOD-like receptor protein 3 ( NLRP3) inflammasome, thereby inducing podocyte pyroptosis. Furthermore, increased gut microbiota dysbiosis,characterized by decreased probiotic diversity and increased pathogenic bacteria, was observed in DN mice. DNase I treatment restored probiotic diversity, highlighting a potential interaction between NETs and gut microbiota in DN progression. Collectively, our findings suggest that NETs critically mediate diabetic podocyte dysfunction through ROS-induced activation of NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis and gut microbiota dysbiosis, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting NETs in DN treatment.

articles.title: Ginkgolide B alleviates granulomatous mastitis with gut microbiota remodeling and altered macrophage responses.
articles.abstract: Granulomatous mastitis (GM) is an inflammatory breast disease linked to Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii, causing pain, abscesses, and reduced quality of life. The gut-mammary axis suggests intestinal homeostasis modulates peripheral immunity. Ginkgolide B (GB), a bioactive diterpene lactone, has anti-inflammatory effects, but its role in GM is unclear. In GM mice, GB significantly alleviated mammary inflammation and fibrosis, reducing cytokines, collagen deposition, and pathological lesions, while also restoring colonic mucosal thickness, Alcian blue-positive mucosal area, and tight-junction proteins (occludin, zonula occludens-1, and claudin-3), consistent with improved barrier-associated features. 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequencing showed GB partially reversed gut dysbiosis, restoring microbial diversity, enriching taxa (Ligilactobacillus, Muribaculaceae), and reducing the disease-associated expansion of genera (Lactobacillus, Dubosiella, Faecalibaculum). Metabolomics identified α-linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism as a key pathway, with ALA and related metabolites recovered after GB treatment, and this shift correlated with microbial remodeling. Antibiotic pretreatment attenuated GB's protective effects, supporting the involvement of the gut microbiota. GB treatment was associated with lower CD80, CD86, and iNOS and higher CD206 expression in whole mammary tissue. Mammary IL-1β, IL-6, and TGF-β1 were reduced, whereas the decrease in TNF-α was not statistically significant. Direct GB treatment also modulated inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 cells, supporting a direct effect of GB on macrophage-related responses. Overall, GB alleviated experimental GM in association with intestinal, microbial, metabolic, and macrophage-related changes, supporting a potential link between gut microbiota-associated metabolic remodeling and macrophage responses.

articles.title: Enabling solid oral dosage design with flexible hybrid dissolution modeling.
articles.abstract: The dissolution of oral solid dosage forms is an important quality attribute that needs to be carefully engineered to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. However, dissolution is a complex physical process that is influenced by multiple factors such as drug substance properties, formulation variables, manufacturing process conditions, and even dissolution testing conditions. Consequently, developing a robust understanding of the system is challenging and experimentally intensive. In this work, we propose a hybrid modeling framework which uses an artificial neural network (ANN) to learn a relationship between various input variables and the parameters of a mechanistic model based on the Noyes-Whitney equation. The hybrid framework offers the flexibility of data-driven approaches, while also enhancing model interpretability and capturing physical aspects of the dissolution process. The use of the framework is demonstrated via two case studies involving modified-release drug products spanning variations in formulation composition in the first and coating composition and weight gain in the second. The results establish its utility within these formulation domains. Although the framework can be deployed for other drug product types and can incorporate manufacturing routes and process conditions as model inputs, its performance in these broader settings remains to be validated. Advanced model deployment in the form of inverse design for generating formulation recommendations and transfer learning of a trained model to a new drug product system is also discussed. Overall, the proposed hybrid framework provides a practical route towards more efficient and informed formulation and process development.

articles.title: Influence of electron-beam irradiation on electrospun PVA nanofiber mats for potential wound-dressing applications.
articles.abstract: Electrospun polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) nanofibers have emerged as promising candidates for advanced wound-dressing applications due to their high porosity, large specific surface area, and structural similarity to the extracellular matrix. However, their intrinsic water solubility necessitates stabilization strategies such as crosslinking to maintain structural integrity in hydrated environments. In this study, PVA nanofiber mats were fabricated using electrospinning under systematically varied processing parameters and subsequently treated with electron-beam irradiation at absorbed doses of 25, 50, 75, and 100 kGy as a physical approach to irradiation-induced polymer-network modification. The influence of electrospinning conditions on fiber morphology and process stability was evaluated, including a qualitative Taylor cone rating system to support reproducibility. The stability of the Taylor cone is known to be a key determinant offiber uniformity and defect formation. Morphological analysis using scanning electron microscopy revealed uniform fibers (∼0.166 μm diameter) with controlled porosity (45-55%), a critical parameter for fluid absorption and gas exchange in wound dressings. Functional characterization included water uptake capacity, layer thickness, and mechanical testing. Electron-beam irradiation preserved the nanofibrous morphology and high water-uptake capacity while producing a clear dose-dependent mechanical response. Among the doses tested, 25 kGy provided the most promising tensile performance, whereas the benefit diminished at higher doses. However, the interpretation of thickness and mechanical data is limited by the inclusion of the aluminum backing during thickness measurements and by tensile testing performed exclusively under dry conditions. The combined response detected is consistent with a favourable balance between irradiation-induced network-forming reactions and chain scission at 25 kGy and supports electron-beam irradiation as apotential post-processing strategy for PVA wound-dressing scaffolds that requires further biological validation.

articles.title: TRIM11 Regulates Filopodia Formation and Cytoskeletal Remodeling Through the N-WASP/ARP2/3 Pathway in Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Filopodia are thin extensions of the plasma membrane that are rich in actin, which helps in cancer cells migration and invasion characters. TRIM11 (Tripartite motif 11), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plays an important part in the progression and advanced stage of colorectal cancer (CRC); however, its role in the remodeling of the cytoskeleton is not well established. This present study explored the role of TRIM11 in regulating filopodia formation and metastatic behavior in CRC cells by bioinformatic, molecular docking and functional analysis. TRIM11 was knocked down in CRC (HCT116) using siRNA targeting TRIM11 and it was validated by western blot analysis. The migration and invasion of CRC cells dramatically impaired by silencing TRIM11 in HCT116 confirmed by trans well invasion assay and Scratch wound healing assay. Moreover, TRIM11 knockdown facilitated autophagy related markers. Reduced expression of antiapoptotic marker (BCL2) and inhibition of EMT (Epithelial to mesenchymal transition) marker further confirmed the enhanced apoptosis and decreased metastatic progression in TRIM11-silenced HCT116 cells. Immunofluorescence investigation validated that TRIM11 silencing impaired the length and quantity of filopodia on the cellular surface. Mechanically, the expression of TRIM11 was found to have a positive correlation with the expression of key modulators involved in the reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton, such as ARP2, ARP3, WAVE2, and N-WASP. Filopodia development in CRC cells was inhibited by the suppression of N-WASP/ARP2/ARP3 pathway.

articles.title: Bisphenol A Aggravates Allergic Rhinitis by Impairing Nasal Epithelial Barrier via AKR1B1 Downregulation: Insights from In Silico and Experimental Evidence.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous environmental pollutant, has increasingly been associated with the development of allergic rhinitis (AR). However, the molecular basis through which BPA contributes to AR remains unclear. Here, an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, multi-level bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation, was applied to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying BPA-mediated development of AR. Analysis of publicly available databases yielded six candidate targets, namely AKR1B1, AKR1C2, ALOX15, FABP6, EP300, and NR3C2. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that these targets are associated with immune imbalance in the nasal mucosa of AR. Among them, AKR1B1 was prioritized as the central target by multiple machine learning algorithms and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Molecular docking suggested a potential BPA-AKR1B1 interaction, and molecular dynamics simulations characterized the conformational stability of the predicted complex under the simulated conditions. Single-cell sequencing analysis localized AKR1B1 primarily to nasal epithelial cells, while virtual knockout analysis highlighted MAPK signaling as the downstream pathway most markedly altered after AKR1B1 deletion. In vivo, BPA exposure exacerbated allergic symptoms, histopathological changes and epithelial barrier disruption in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced AR mice model and further decreased AKR1B1 expression in the nasal mucosa. In vitro, BPA reduced tight junction protein expression, including ZO-1 and occludin, in human nasal epithelial cells (HNEpCs), whereas AKR1B1 overexpression partially rescued this BPA-induced barrier damage. Furthermore, knockdown of AKR1B1 activated the MAPK signaling pathway in HNEpCs. Collectively, these results suggest that BPA may facilitate AR progression by impairing nasal epithelial barrier integrity, potentially through the AKR1B1/MAPK axis. The present study expands current understanding of the toxicological mechanisms linking BPA exposure to AR and provides a mechanistic basis for developing intervention strategies.

articles.title: Molecular mechanisms of diethyl phthalate enhanced invasion in gastric cancer revealed by integrative network toxicology machine learning and in vitro analyses.
articles.abstract: Diethyl phthalate (DEP) is a ubiquitous environmental endocrine-disrupting chemical to which human populations are widely exposed. Increasing evidence links DEP to the malignant progression of solid tumors; however, the key molecular networks and experimentally validated mechanisms underlying DEP-enhanced invasion in gastric cancer (GC) remain largely undefined. Four transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus were integrated to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to determine tumor-associated key modules. Potential DEP targets were predicted using multiple databases and intersected with-related DEGs and key module genes to define core candidate genes. Functional enrichment and network analyses were then performed. Subsequently, a multi-model ensemble machine learning framework combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based interpretability was applied to prioritize candidate genes. Molecular docking was used to evaluate the potential binding affinity between DEP and key target proteins. Finally, the effects of DEP on oxidative stress, migration and invasion, cytoskeletal remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) were experimentally validated in AGS and HGC-27 cells. Thirteen core candidate genes were identified. Functional enrichment analyses primarily implicated lysosomal proteolysis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and chromatin remodeling and epigenetic regulation. Among the evaluated machine learning models, the gradient boosting machine (GBM) model demonstrated the best overall diagnostic performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of an additional random forest model highlighted CTSB, PLAU, ALDH3A1, ATAD2, and CBX7 as influential features for GC classification. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between DEP and these candidate proteins. In vitro experiments demonstrated that DEP exposure increased intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and promoted cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in AGS and HGC-27 cells. These effects were accompanied by filamentous actin (F-actin) reorganization, increased RhoA and MLC1 expression, decreased E-cadherin expression, and increased N-cadherin and vimentin expression, consistent with EMT-related alterations. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that DEP exposure enhances invasion-related malignant phenotypes in gastric cancer cells and identify candidate molecular targets potentially associated with GC progression. Although network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking provide complementary evidence for target prioritization, further functional studies are required to determine whether these candidate targets directly mediate DEP-induced cellular effects.

articles.title: Calycosin attenuates a TGF-β-responsive COL3A1-associated fibroblast program in non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast-derived extracellular-matrix programs are prominent in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but bulk transcriptomic signals do not identify the relevant cellular compartment or establish whether candidate stromal programs respond to defined compounds. We integrated cell-resolved multi-omics analyses with fibroblast perturbation experiments to prioritize an Astragalus-associated stromal program and test its response to calycosin. A systematic public-data workflow integrated curated compound-target relationships with transcriptomic, co-expression, proteomic, single-cell, microenvironmental, dependency, protein-interaction, perturbational, and ranking-robustness evidence. Experimental validation used four independent biological repeats in TGF-β1-activated MRC-5 human lung fibroblasts together with a minimal four-donor primary NSCLC CAF validation set, with calycosin, the TGF-β receptor inhibitor SB431542, and COL3A1 loss- and gain-of-function perturbations. A separate concentration-response experiment evaluated calycosin at 5, 10, and 25 µM, with molecular, signaling, viability, and conditioned-medium effects on A549 and NCI-H520 spheroid invasion assessed across the dose range. The formal cross-cohort intersection identified four candidates shared by LUAD and LUSC-MMP1, MMP9, COL3A1, and PPARG. COL3A1 had concordant RNA-protein support, fibroblast-enriched single-cell expression, and recurrent associations with CAF signatures. In the principal TGF-β1-activated MRC-5 experiment, 25 µM calycosin reduced COL3A1 expression from 4.57- to 2.50-fold, collagen III secretion from 3.82 to 2.26 ng/105 cells/16 h, the α-SMA-high fraction from 64.5% to 33.5%, and CAGA activity from 4.14- to 2.38-fold. In a separate four-repeat dose series (0, 5, 10, and 25 µM), the means of eight molecular and functional endpoints declined with dose; paired-repeat linear-dose slopes were negative (two-sided P = 9.83 × 10-6 to 2.71 × 10-4), although not every replicate decreased strictly at 5 µM. In GSE153935, COL3A1 was enriched in fibroblasts (7/7 evaluable matched donors; exact signed-rank P = 0.0156). All four primary CAF donors showed a reduction in COL3A1, ACTA2, and conditioned-medium-driven A549 invasion with calycosin, but none of the three contrasts met the familywise Holm threshold (adjusted P = 0.0679). At the highest dose, MRC-5 live-cell fractions and tumor-spheroid viability were modestly reduced, so a viability-related contribution to invasion outcomes cannot be excluded. COL3A1 knockdown reduced selected activation endpoints and overexpression partly restored A549 invasion under calycosin treatment. Public cohort data, an independent single-cell dataset and perturbation experiments in MRC-5 fibroblasts support a calycosin-responsive, TGF-β-associated fibroblast phenotype marked by COL3A1. Four primary NSCLC CAF cultures showed the same direction of effect, but none of the calycosin comparisons remained significant after multiplicity adjustment, so these data are preliminary. COL3A1 perturbation altered selected fibroblast-conditioned readouts. Direct calycosin-COL3A1 binding, exclusive mediation, and a toxicity-independent anti-invasive effect remain to be tested.

articles.title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

articles.title: Prokinetic effect of ferulic acid ethyl ester on gastrointestinal motility in mice: an integrated in silico and in vivo study.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal paralysis and dysmotility remain clinically relevant conditions associated with delayed intestinal transit, feeding intolerance, prolonged hospitalization, and limited effective pharmacological treatment options. Among these disorders, postoperative ileus (POI) is a common complication after abdominal surgery characterized by transient suppression of coordinated gastrointestinal motility. The present study investigated the effects of ferulic acid ethyl ester (FAEE) on intestinal motility and explored its underlying mechanisms using integrated in silico and in vivo approaches. Gastrointestinal transit was assessed in mice by the charcoal meal test under normal conditions and in an experimental POI model induced by intestinal manipulation. In normal mice, FAEE (50 and 100 mg/kg, p.o.) significantly increased intestinal transit. In POI animals, FAEE (50 mg/kg) significantly attenuated the postoperative delay in intestinal transit. Biochemical analyses showed that FAEE reduced MPO activity, NOx, and MDA levels, while restoring SOD activity and GSH content. Pharmacological studies further indicated that the prokinetic effect of FAEE involves cholinergic and calcium-dependent pathways, as atropine and verapamil significantly attenuated its effects. In contrast, pharmacological blockade of opioid and 5-HT3 receptors did not significantly alter the prokinetic effect of FAEE under the present experimental conditions. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of FAEE to M3R and CaV1.2. In conclusion, FAEE exerts prokinetic effects and attenuates the development of postoperative dysmotility, with findings suggesting the involvement of cholinergic and calcium-dependent pathways and an association with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.

articles.title: Proanthocyanidin ameliorates BCCAO-induced neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) in rats by targeting NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome pathway.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a major cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability, characterized by excessive oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal degeneration following the restoration of cerebral blood flow. The present study investigated the neuroprotective effects of proanthocyanidin (PAC) against bilateral common carotid artery occlusion (BCCAO)-induced cerebral ischemia in Wistar albino rats, with particular emphasis on the NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathway. Rats subjected to BCCAO received PAC at two dose levels or standard therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel). Neurological and cognitive functions were evaluated using the rotarod, actophotometer, and elevated plus maze tests. Biochemical assays were performed to determine oxidative stress markers and antioxidant enzyme activities, while histopathological examination assessed neuronal integrity. The molecular mechanism was further investigated by Western blot analysis and densitometric quantification of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 protein expression. BCCAO significantly impaired motor coordination, locomotor activity, and memory retention, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, myeloperoxidase, and acetylcholinesterase activities, depletion of endogenous antioxidants (glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and catalase), and marked neuronal degeneration in the hippocampal and cortical regions. PAC treatment significantly improved behavioral performance, restored antioxidant defense, reduced oxidative stress and biochemical alterations, and preserved neuronal architecture in a dose-dependent manner. Western blot analysis demonstrated that PAC markedly downregulated the overexpression of NF-κB (p65), NLRP3, and caspase-1 proteins, indicating suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation. Overall, PAC exhibited significant neuroprotective efficacy comparable to aspirin plus clopidogrel, suggesting that its beneficial effects are mediated through the attenuation of oxidative stress and the inhibition of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling. These findings support PAC as a promising phytotherapeutic candidate for the management of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Disproportionality analysis of ventricular extrasystoles reported with semaglutide in VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System.
articles.abstract: Semaglutide is widely used to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and to reduce cardiovascular risk. However, its association with cardiac rhythm-related adverse-event reporting in routine clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. To investigate cardiovascular and rhythm-related adverse-event reporting associated with semaglutide, with a focus on ventricular extrasystoles, we conducted a disproportionality analysis of individual case safety reports from VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS; formerly the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System [FAERS]). Reports were included when semaglutide was recorded as a suspected drug, according to database-specific criteria. Cardiovascular outcomes were identified using Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Preferred Terms. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. A cross-database reporting signal was defined as at least three semaglutide-associated reports and a lower 95% CI bound exceeding 1 in each database. After deduplication and application of the predefined inclusion criteria, 1980 semaglutide-associated cardiovascular reports from VigiBase and 1754 from AEMS were included. Among the screened cardiovascular and rhythm-related preferred terms, ventricular extrasystoles was the only term that met the prespecified signal criterion in both databases. Ventricular extrasystoles, clinically corresponding to premature ventricular contractions, showed disproportionate reporting in VigiBase (ROR 1.77, 95% CI 1.31-2.40) and AEMS (ROR 1.37, 95% CI 1.00-1.88; unrounded lower CI bound > 1). Ventricular extrasystoles showed a consistent disproportionality signal across VigiBase and AEMS. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish incidence, causality, or prognostic significance, this finding warrants prospective investigation using systematic electrocardiographic assessment and ambulatory rhythm monitoring.

articles.title: Potential association between IL-12/23, IL-23, and IL-17 inhibitors and skin cancer: a pharmacovigilance study based on the FAERS database.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Interleukin (IL)-12/23, IL-23, and IL-17 inhibitors are increasingly used for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, yet their long-term risk of skin cancer remains unclear due to limited evidence from randomized controlled trials. METHODS: We conducted a disproportionality analysis using individual case safety reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004 to 2025 Q2. Reporting odds ratios (ROR) and information components (IC) were calculated to assess the association between IL-12/23, IL-23, and IL-17 inhibitors and skin cancer. Subgroup analyses by age and sex, time-to-onset analysis, Weibull modeling, and co-medication interaction analysis were further performed. RESULTS: A total of 3,661 skin cancer reports were identified. Significant disproportionality signals were observed for most interleukin inhibitors, with the strongest associations for risankizumab (ROR 8.01, 95% CI 7.62-8.42; IC025, 2.88), tildrakizumab (ROR 5.81, 95% CI 4.13-8.19; IC025, 1.84), and ustekinumab (ROR 5.53, 95% CI 5.23-5.85, IC025, 2.35). IL-17 inhibitors showed weaker signals and were no longer significant in psoriasis-restricted sensitivity analyses. The association was more pronounced in elderly patients, especially for those aged >75 years. Weibull analysis indicated a wear-out failure pattern for ustekinumab and risankizumab, suggesting an increasing reporting frequency over time. Co-medication analyses did not reveal significant synergistic reporting signals. CONCLUSION: This pharmacovigilance study identified disproportionate reporting of skin cancer in reports involving IL-12/23 and IL-23 inhibitors, particularly risankizumab and ustekinumab, with weaker signals for IL-17 inhibitors. These findings represent signal detection from a spontaneous reporting database and highlight the need for dermatological monitoring in high-risk patients, warranting further prospective investigation to clarify clinical significance.

articles.title: Refining absolute GFR estimation in children: development and validation of the GROW-GFR equation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate estimation of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is essential when dosing many medications. Existing paediatric GFR equations vary in accuracy, with only one (Modified Schwartz) validated in children <2 years. This study developed a new paediatric GFR equation (GROW-GFR) using a tobramycin population pharmacokinetic model and evaluated its performance against current equations and nuclear medicine (NM)-GFR scans. METHODS: Retrospective analysis of NM-GFR scans from July 2016-November 2023 in children aged 0-19 years at The Royal Children's Hospital, Melbourne. Results were included if NM-GFR was ≤150 mL/min and height, weight and serum creatinine were recorded. Accuracy of GFR estimates within 30% and 10% of NM-GFR results (p30, p10 accuracy) and bias for the GROW-GFR, Modified Schwartz, Chronic Kidney Disease in Children Under 25 years (CKiD-U25), Full Age Spectrum (FAS), and FAS-height (HT) equations were assessed. RESULTS: Overall, 1560 NM-GFR results from 711 children (median age 8.5 years; range 0.1-19) were included (median NM-GFR 55 mL/min; range 0.5-150). GROW-GFR showed a p30 accuracy of 76% and bias of -1.9 mL/min, with consistent performance across all ages. The Modified Schwartz equation had a p30 accuracy of 46% and bias of 17.3 mL/min. In children ≥2 years, GROW-GFR outperformed other equations (p30: 76% vs. 49%-58%; bias -1.9 vs. 13.7-18.4 mL/min). After applying linear mixed-effects models, GROW-GFR p30 accuracy and bias were 80% and -2.5 mL/min, outperforming other equations (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The GROW-GFR equation provided more accurate GFR estimates across all paediatric ages, including children <2 years, compared to existing equations. Therefore, should be considered the preferred GFR estimation method.

articles.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury. METHODS: Network pharmacology was used to screen quercetin's therapeutic targets for GDM. Molecular docking was performed using the human RAGE structure to predict the potential interaction between quercetin and RAGE, and molecular dynamics simulation was conducted to evaluate the stability of the predicted complex. A combined streptozotocin-high-fat diet GDM rat model and 30 mM high-glucose HTR-8/SVneo trophoblast injury model were constructed. FPS-ZM1 was used as a pharmacological tool to perturb RAGE-associated signaling in vitro. ROS, inflammatory cytokines, and key pathway gene and protein expression were examined to characterize the associated signaling changes. RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified SERPINE1 (a critical regulator of placental vascular remodeling) as the core hub gene, with the AGE-RAGE pathway showing the highest enrichment score. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a dynamically stable complex formed between quercetin and the ligand-binding domain of RAGE. GDM induction was associated with increased AGE accumulation, RAGE expression, ROS production, phosphorylated NF-κB p65, and SERPINE1 expression, together with an increase in Nrf2 expression, whereas quercetin treatment attenuated these alterations. Quercetin intervention also improved glucose tolerance and placental pathological changes. CONCLUSION: Quercetin alleviates GDM-associated placental dysfunction by improving metabolic abnormalities, oxidative imbalance, and inflammatory responses. Computational analysis suggests a potential interaction between quercetin and RAGE. These findings provide evidence that quercetin may regulate the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network and improve placental homeostasis under diabetic conditions.

articles.title: Time-varying metoprolol exposure and the risk of acute kidney injury: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding the association between metoprolol use and acute kidney injury (AKI) remains limited, particularly because of time-varying exposure, cardiovascular confounding, and uncertain temporal ordering. We evaluated the association between recent metoprolol exposure and incident AKI using a longitudinal time-varying framework. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective longitudinal cohort study included adult inpatients from three Chinese hospitals between January 2020 and December 2024. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate ≥60 mL min-1·1.73 m-2 at cohort entry and sufficient serial serum creatinine (Scr) and medication execution records. Metoprolol was modeled as a lag-1 time-varying exposure, relating use on hospital day t to AKI risk on day t+1. Incident AKI was identified using rolling KDIGO Scr criteria. Time-varying Cox regression adjusted for demographic characteristics, baseline renal function, major comorbidities, baseline severity-related factors, and lagged concomitant medication exposures. Sensitivity and complementary analyses evaluated the robustness of the findings. RESULTS: Among 291,049 screened hospitalizations, 20,333 patients contributed 284,470 risk intervals, and 1,050 developed incident AKI. Lag-1 metoprolol exposure was associated with a higher AKI hazard in the unadjusted model (HR, 2.53; 95% CI, 2.13-3.00). The association was substantially attenuated after adjustment but remained statistically significant in the primary model (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.79; P = 0.022). Prespecified follow-up-time analyses suggested that the association was concentrated during the first 72 h after cohort entry. Sensitivity analyses generally yielded estimates in the same direction, although the magnitude and statistical significance varied across analytical specifications; the association was attenuated to non-significance in the 2-day lag analysis (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 0.96-1.68) and after additional adjustment for vasopressor use (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.98-1.70). No consistent monotonic dose-response relationship was observed. CONCLUSION: Recent metoprolol exposure was associated with a modestly higher hazard of incident AKI in the primary adjusted analysis. However, attenuation after adjustment, temporal heterogeneity, sensitivity to exposure timing and confounding control, and the absence of a consistent monotonic dose-response pattern suggest that residual confounding and clinical treatment context may contribute to the observed association. These findings should be interpreted as a hypothesis-generating short-term AKI safety signal rather than evidence of direct metoprolol nephrotoxicity or causality.

articles.title: Kurarinol A from Sophora flavescens suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sophora flavescens is traditionally used in TCM and Miao/Mongolian/Yi ethnomedicines for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anti-hepatic fibrosis efficacy, mechanism, and target of the ethyl acetate fraction (EAF) from S. flavescens and its key lavandulyl flavonoid kurarinol A (KA). METHODS: A CCl4-induced mouse hepatic fibrosis model was established to evaluate liver injury and fibrosis by H&E/Masson staining and detection of serum ALT/AST and hepatic α-SMA/fibronectin/Hyp. A TGF-β1-activated LX-2 cell model was established, with cell viability, migration, and apoptosis evaluated by MTS, wound-healing, and Annexin V-FITC/PI assays. Transcriptomics, KEGG analysis, molecular docking, Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, CETSA, and MyD88 knockdown/overexpression assays were applied to explore the underlying mechanism. RESULTS: In vivo, EAF (50 and 100 mg/kg) alleviated CCl4-induced liver injury and fibrosis and decreased the levels of fibrotic serum biomarkers. In vitro, KA significantly inhibited LX-2 cell activation with an IC50 of 12.65 μM (n = 3), suppressing cell proliferation and migration while inducing apoptosis. KA's anti-fibrotic activity was validated only in vitro, and its contribution to the in vivo efficacy of the EAF remains inferred rather than directly proven. Mechanistically, KA downregulated key signaling molecules of the TLR4/NF-κB pathway, thereby blocking pathway activation. Molecular docking, MD simulations and CETSA supported a direct interaction between KA and MyD88. MyD88 knockdown and overexpression assays further supported that MyD88 serves as a candidate molecular target mediating KA's anti-fibrotic activity. CONCLUSION: The EAF exerts anti-fibrotic effects in vivo, and KA exhibits consistent anti-fibrotic activity in vitro. These findings support MyD88 as a potential molecular target mediating KA's in vitro anti-fibrotic activity via TLR4/NF-κB signaling. These findings not only validate the traditional use of S. flavescens in hepatobiliary disorders, but also offer a promising MyD88-targeting candidate warranting lead optimization for anti-fibrotic drug development.

articles.title: Knowledge distillation-based rapid identification of Ligustici Rhizoma et Radix decoction piece varieties.
articles.abstract: UNLABELLED: To address the commingling of different varieties of Ligusticum decoction pieces in the market and the difficulty of achieving rapid, efficient, and accurate on-site identification, this study aimed to develop a lightweight deep learning model that combines high identification accuracy with fast inference speed. METHODS: Images of six categories of Ligusticum decoction pieces and their adulterants were acquired in an enclosed photographic light box to construct a standardized image dataset. Using ImageNet-pretrained weights, several high-accuracy models were selected as teacher models through comparative model evaluation, and knowledge distillation was subsequently employed to optimize the lightweight MobileNetV2 model as the student model. Finally, an interactive identification application was developed using PyQt5. RESULTS: After knowledge distillation, the MobileNetV2 model achieved an identification accuracy of 99.73%, approaching the accuracy of the teacher models. Meanwhile, the distilled model contained only 2.23 million parameters, substantially fewer than the teacher models, thereby achieving both high identification accuracy and ease of deployment. CONCLUSION: The lightweight identification model developed in this study efficiently extracted high-level discriminative features from images of Ligusticum decoction pieces and their adulterants, enabling rapid and accurate identification and providing a feasible technical approach for the rapid on-site authentication of traditional Chinese medicine decoction pieces.

articles.title: Peppermint oil exhibits antispasmodic and anti-inflammatory properties and alters gut microbial community composition and gas production in vitro.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peppermint oil (PMO) is an herbal medicinal product used for the symptomatic relief of minor spasms of the gastrointestinal tract, flatulence and abdominal pain, especially in patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). To gain a more comprehensive understanding of the multimodal effects of PMO in IBS, the investigations aimed to confirm its antispasmodic and anti-inflammatory effects and assess direct effects of PMO on the human gut microbiome and microbial gas production in vitro. METHODS: To investigate the spasmolytic activity of PMO (BNO 2910), circular smooth muscle strips from the proximal colon of five male guinea pigs were used. Its anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated using RAW 264.7 macrophages stimulated with LPS. TNF secretion and nitrite levels, as an indicator of NO production, were measured using ELISA and Griess reagent, respectively. Effects on the human gut microbiome and colonic fermentation activity were assessed in an anaerobic in vitro fermentation system inoculated with stool samples from six healthy donors using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, flow cytometry-based cell counting and gas production measurements. RESULTS: PMO showed antispasmodic effects on isolated smooth muscle strips of guinea pig colon tissue as well as inhibition of LPS-induced TNF secretion and NO induction in RAW 264.7 macrophages. Additionally, PMO significantly reduced microbial gas production in stool samples from healthy donors, indicating reduced microbial fermentation activity under the experimental conditions, while the alpha diversity indices richness and evenness were maintained or even increased. At the genus level, PMO showed direct effects on microbiome community composition, inhibiting the growth of potential disease-related organisms (e.g., Escherichia-Shigella or Eggerthella), while maintaining or even increasing the abundance of health-related organisms (e.g., Blautia and Faecalibacterium). CONCLUSION: Besides antispasmodic and anti-inflammatory effects, PMO exhibits direct effects on the human gut microbiome, including the modulation of microbial communities and total gas production in vitro. To determine the specific relevance of the observed microbiome-related effects of PMO in IBS further disease-specific studies are warranted.

articles.title: The integrin αvβ6/TGF-β1/Smad4 signaling pathway regulates ENaC in alcohol induced ARDS.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by impaired alveolar-capillary permeability and pulmonary edema. Alveolar fluid clearance (AFC) is strongly associated with patient prognosis. This study aimed to investigate whether chronic alcohol consumption affects sodium channel regulation in ARDS via the Integrin αvβ6/TGF-β1/Smad4 signaling pathway. METHODS: We established chronic alcohol exposure models in mice and MLE-12 cells, followed by lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ARDS in both systems. The Integrin αvβ6/TGF-β1/Smad4 pathway was inhibited to explore its regulatory effect on ENaC and Na+,K+-ATPase during alcohol-induced ARDS. RESULTS: We found that chronic alcohol consumption exacerbated lung injury by activating this signaling pathway, which suppressed ENaC and Na+,K+-ATPase protein expression. Inhibition of the pathway alleviated pulmonary edema and inflammation and improved survival rates. Both in vivo and in vitro results demonstrated that the Integrin αvβ6/TGF-β1/Smad4 pathway regulates ENaC and Na+,K+-ATPase in alcohol-induced ARDS. CONCLUSION: These findings may clarify the regulatory mechanisms of sodium channels in ARDS associated with chronic alcohol consumption.

articles.title: Defining kratom: evidence-based policy guidelines for a rapidly evolving market.
articles.abstract: The leaves of Mitragyna speciosa, commonly called kratom, have been consumed for centuries in Southeast Asia for their energizing and analgesic properties. Over the last decade kratom has gained popularity in the United States, with an estimated 10-16 million consumers, and a wide variety of products have become available in the marketplace. Along with a plethora of product formulations that contain various concentrations of kratom alkaloids, new products have emerged, labelled as "kratom", but comprised of highly concentrated synthetic alkaloids. Consumers and regulators alike struggle to differentiate the spectrum of products that range from those similar in composition to traditional kratom to those that are illegally marketed, unapproved novel drugs. With significant implications to public health policy and safety, there is a need to clearly define and differentiate kratom, kratom-derived, and synthetic products. Herein we offer guidance to support standardization of the terminology used in the manufacture and labelling of kratom and kratom-derived products in the United States. This is intended to be a reference tool for use by industry and federal, state, and other jurisdictions that oversee the kratom industry to encourage clear and consistent communication.

articles.title: Calycosin alleviates myocardial injury in diabetic mice by enhancing lipophagy in cardiomyocytes via Rab7a regulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major life-threatening cardiovascular complication of diabetes mellitus, characterized by myocardial lipid deposition, lipotoxicity and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Impaired lipophagy-the selective autophagic clearance of lipid droplets (LDs)-is a key driver of DCM progression, and Rab7a, a small GTPase, is essential for autophagosome-lysosome fusion, the rate-limiting step of efficient lipophagic degradation. Calycosin (CA), a natural isoflavone derived from Astragalus membranaceus, exerts antidiabetic and cardioprotective effects. However, whether CA regulates lipophagy via Ras-related protein Rab-7a (Rab7a) to ameliorate DCM remains largely unknown. The present study investigated whether CA alleviates DCM by promoting lipophagy through Rab7a-dependent mechanisms. METHODS: In vivo, DCM was induced in male C57BL/6J mice by a high-fat diet combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ), followed by daily CA administration. In vitro, neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) were isolated and exposed to high glucose and high lipid (HGHL) conditions to mimic the DCM microenvironment. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. Myocardial lipid accumulation was evaluated by Oi-Red O staining, Bodipy staining and triglyceride (TG) quantification assay. Lipophagy was monitored using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), LC3-LD colocalization analysis and Western blotting. Rab7a was knocked down in NMCMs using specific small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), and its ubiquitination level was detected by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay. RESULTS: CA significantly improved cardiac function, reduced myocardial fibrosis and lipid accumulation, and restored impaired lipophagic flux in DCM mice. Consistently, in HGHL-stimulated NMCMs, CA promoted lipophagy and suppressed lipotoxic injury. Mechanistically, CA upregulated Rab7a protein expression and inhibited its ubiquitination. Rab7a knockdown abolished CA-mediated lipophagy activation and subsequent lipid clearance. CONCLUSION: CA enhances cardiomyocyte lipophagy by upregulating Rab7a and suppressing its ubiquitination, thereby mitigating excessive lipid deposition and subsequent myocardial injury in DCM mice. These findings reveal a novel mechanism by which CA regulates cardiomyocyte lipophagy and highlight Rab7a-mediated lipophagy as a promising therapeutic target for diabetic cardiac lipotoxicity.

articles.title: Ferroptosis, mitochondrial stress and redox imbalance: a pharmacological-toxicological biochemistry framework for precision drug therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, mitochondrial stress and redox imbalance are increasingly recognised as interconnected determinants of therapeutic efficacy, drug resistance and organ toxicity. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and impaired antioxidant defences, with relevance to cancer, cardiovascular disease, inflammatory disorders, ischaemia-reperfusion injury and drug-induced tissue damage. This Perspective reframes the ferroptosis-mitochondrial stress-redox axis as a unified pharmacological-toxicological platform rather than an isolated therapeutic target, resolving its mechanisms to individual electron transport chain complexes, membrane phospholipid species and downstream immunological consequences. Beyond the conventional GPX4-system Xc-NRF2 framework, we incorporate dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), GCH1-BH4 signalling, NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy and p53-dependent regulation of ferroptosis sensitivity. We further define how complex I- and III-derived superoxide, compartmentalised inner-membrane lipid pools and ACSL4/LPCAT3-directed phospholipid remodelling shape organ-specific vulnerability. Because ferroptotic cells release damage-associated molecular patterns whose effects depend on cell death kinetics, immunomodulation is considered a distinct therapeutic opportunity and safety consideration. To consolidate these interacting mechanisms into a single, comprehensible reference, we present an integrated molecular pathway diagram that maps oxidative-stress chemistry, compartment-resolved mitochondrial involvement, lipid-substrate specificity, cell-death execution and kinetics-dependent immunological crosstalk onto their corresponding pharmacological entry points. We propose a tiered biomarker framework, a p53-and biomarker-guided patient stratification strategy, a chemically stratified therapeutic map distinguishing repurposed drugs from experimental compounds, and a conceptual pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic framework linking therapeutic and toxic exposure windows. Future research should prioritise biomarker validation, complex-specific mitochondrial functional assays, lipidomic profiling, organ-specific toxicology, tumour-selective delivery systems and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic integration to advance safer, more precise ferroptosis-based therapeutics.

articles.title: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics testing in clinical practice: A pilot implementation in Singapore.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics (PPGx) testing holds promise for optimizing drug therapy, but uptake remains limited in Asia. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of PPGx uptake into clinical practice and its impact on prescribing in an Asian healthcare setting. METHODS: A prospective, multicentre pilot study was conducted to pre-emptively genotype 16 pharmacogenes. Results were integrated into electronic health records, alongside deployment of clinical decision support (CDS) tools for 31 drug-gene pairs. A pharmacogenomics drug information service and digital platforms were also developed. RESULTS: All 2492 participants carried ≥1 actionable variant (median: 5, range: 1-11). Across four institutions within one cluster, 1046 out of 2238 (46.7%) patients were prescribed ≥1 drug with pharmacogenetic association, and of those, 460 (44%) had genotypes linked to undesirable drug responses. Among 285 interruptive CDS alerts, 69 (24.2%) led to prescription modifications. Acceptance was higher for new prescriptions (50.0% vs. 17.3%, p < 0.001), in outpatient settings (31.0% vs. 7.3%, p < 0.001) and among consultants (57.1% vs. other designations 5-27.3%, p < 0.001). The drug information service received 137 enquiries, while 471 and 151 patients accessed the app and web-based platforms respectively. CONCLUSIONS: PPGx testing and genotype-guided prescribing are feasible in Singapore. Widespread adoption requires leadership support, robust informatics infrastructure, clinician engagement and sustainable funding.

articles.title: Renal Function-Guided Valganciclovir Dosing and Ganciclovir Exposure Variability: A Population Pharmacokinetic Simulation Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ganciclovir (GCV) exposure after standard valganciclovir (VGCV) prophylaxis is highly variable. Guidelines recommend Cockcroft-Gault for renal dose adjustment. We evaluated whether Cockcroft-Gault-based dosing achieves the target prophylactic exposure (AUC0-24h: 40-60 mg.h/L) and whether MDRD or CKD-EPI alters exposure. METHODS: Using a validated population pharmacokinetic model, we simulated 10 000 adult solid organ transplant recipients. VGCV doses were assigned according to SmPC renal function categories based on Cockcroft-Gault, MDRD or CKD-EPI. Patient reclassification, target attainment and exposure around dosing thresholds (25, 40 and 60 mL/min) were assessed. RESULTS: MDRD and CKD-EPI reclassified 45.1% and 39.9% of patients, mostly downward, lowering target attainment (20.1% and 22.7% vs. 30.8% with Cockcroft-Gault). Target attainment never exceeded 40% in any category, and underexposure predominated, reaching up to 94.1% in the most impaired renal function categories. Target attainment was consistently lower just below each threshold, and the 25 and 40 mL/min thresholds were set above the renal function ranges where the corresponding regimens achieved target exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Renal function category-based VGCV dosing does not reliably achieve target GCV exposure. Current thresholds are poorly aligned with the exposure-response relationship and warrant re-examination. Alternative equations do not reduce the variability, supporting exposure-guided approaches such as therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing.

articles.title: Integrated In Vitro Characterization of Estrogen Receptor-Mediated Activity, Rapid ERK Signaling, and Steroidogenic Effects of 4-Hydroxybenzophenone.
articles.abstract: 4-Hydroxybenzophenone (4OH-BP) has demonstrated estrogenic activity, but its effects across complementary endocrine pathways remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated estrogen receptor (ER) transcriptional activity, ER antagonist sensitivity, ER-positive cell proliferation, rapid ERK signaling, immediate-early gene expression, and steroidogenesis using an integrated in vitro approach. 4OH-BP induced concentration-dependent ER-mediated transcriptional activity but did not antagonize 17β-estradiol (E2)-induced ER transcriptional activity. Fulvestrant (ICI), a selective ER antagonist, markedly reduced 4OH-BP and E2-induced transcriptional responses, supporting the involvement of classical ER signaling in the transcriptional activity of 4OH-BP. Consistent with its ER-mediated activity, 4OH-BP increased proliferation in ER-positive MCF-7 cells. In rapid-signaling experiments, 4OH-BP induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation, however, the response at 15min was not significantly suppressed by ICI, suggesting that an additional ICI-insensitive signaling component may contribute to the observed response. Changes in the immediate-early genes EGR1 and FOS were temporally associated with the rapid signaling response. In H295R cells, 4OH-BP altered the expression of steroidogenic genes and increased E2 production. Overall, these findings support a multi-endpoint estrogenic profile of 4OH-BP involving classical ER-mediated transcriptional activity, rapid ERK signaling, proliferative responses, and modulation of steroidogenesis. By integrating these complementary endpoints, this in vitro framework provides a broader mechanistic view of 4OH-BP estrogenic activity beyond receptor transactivation alone and may provide a more informative basis for endocrine hazard characterization and chemical prioritization.

articles.title: Dose- and Time-Responsive Genes Identify SFN-Mediated p53 Signaling in Paraquat-Induced Apoptosis and Acute Lung Injury.
articles.abstract: Traditional studies of chemical toxicity mechanisms rely on phenotypic characterization and gene-function experiments, which can delay the identification of targets for intervention. Toxicogenomic data provide a systematic view of chemical responses but contain redundant information that complicates the prioritization of key pathways. In this study, dose- and time-response modeling was used to identify dose-responsive genes (DRGs) and time-responsive genes (TRGs) for focused mechanistic analysis. Enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses of these gene sets prioritized stratifin (SFN) and p53 signaling in paraquat (PQ)-induced acute lung injury. Cellular and mouse-lung experiments supported a model in which PQ-induced SFN upregulation promotes p53 signaling and apoptosis. In mice, PFT-α attenuated pulmonary apoptosis-related changes and histopathological injury, while lung delivery of SFN siRNA attenuated p53 and downstream apoptosis-related responses. These findings support the involvement of the SFN-p53-apoptosis pathway in PQ-induced acute lung injury. The principal contribution is an exposure-response-based strategy to reduce transcriptomic redundancy and prioritize targets and pathways for biological testing.

articles.title: Assessment of Allometric Scaling Methods for the Prediction of Human Pharmacokinetic of LNA-i-miR-221.
articles.abstract: Antisense oligonucleotides are small synthetic DNA or RNA molecules that can be used to modulate gene expression, particularly to block the production of unwanted proteins. This makes them potentially powerful drugs to contrast cancer growth. Drug development is a long process that includes preclinical and clinical studies. Preclinical animal studies are designed to assess drug kinetics and safety before progressing to clinical trials, as they may predict the therapeutic dose to be used in the "first in human" (FIH) studies. This is usually achieved by applying allometric scaling methods that allow predicting the human pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters from those estimated in animals. Selecting the appropriate scaling formula reduces the risk of translational uncertainty and supports the design of FIH studies. The aim of this study is to compare the accuracy of different allometric scaling methods in predicting human PK of the antisense oligonucleotide LNA-i-miR-221, a powerful inhibitor of microRNA miR-221, which was found to be deregulated in several malignancies, favoring cancer progression. To do that, we exploited the availability of PK data of the drug in both Sprague Dawley rats and humans and we found that the best scaling method for both clearance and distribution volume is the simple allometry, with predictions laying within the 2-fold and 4-fold error interval, respectively. This study contributes to identifying the most accurate scaling methods among the evaluated single-species approaches to extrapolate human pharmacokinetic for LNA-i-miR-221, possibly offering a starting point for future studies involving antisense oligonucleotides.

articles.title: N-Benzyl Indole-Benzoxazole Hybrids as Multi-Target Anticancer Agents Modulating mTOR, Apoptosis, and Lipid Dynamics in Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Indole-benzoxazole hybrids are structurally versatile scaffolds with significant promise in anticancer drug development. This study aimed to synthesize N-benzyl-substituted indole-benzoxazole derivatives (IBB1-5) and to evaluate their antiproliferative potential and mechanistic effects in human breast cancer models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: IBB1-5 were synthesized and screened for cytotoxic activity against MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells using MTT assays. The most active compound, IBB-4, was further investigated in MDA-MB-231 cells through clonogenic assays and morphological analysis. Immunofluorescence staining was performed to assess mTOR, LC3, caspase-3, and β-tubulin expression and distribution. Lipid droplet dynamics were evaluated using Oil Red O and Nile Red staining, combined with three-dimensional surface-plot analysis. RESULTS: IBB-4 demonstrated the strongest growth-inhibitory activity, with IC50 values of 12.2 μM (MDA-MB-231) and 12.8 μM (MCF-7). Clonogenic assays revealed significant dose-dependent suppression of long-term proliferative capacity. Morphological alterations included cytoplasmic vacuolization and structural disorganization. Immunofluorescence analyses showed a marked downregulation of mTOR and a spatial redistribution of LC3, without significant changes in total fluorescence intensity. Increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity and pronounced disruption of β-tubulin indicated activation of apoptotic pathways and cytoskeletal destabilization. Lipid staining, supported by three-dimensional surface analysis, demonstrated prominent clustering and redistribution of intracellular lipid droplets. CONCLUSION: IBB-4 exerts multi-layered anticancer effects through coordinated modulation of proliferative signaling, apoptotic activation, cytoskeletal integrity, and lipid compartmentalization. These findings identify IBB-4 as a promising lead candidate for further molecular and preclinical investigations, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer.

articles.title: Safety profile of desmopressin and risk signals for hyponatremia: evidence from FAERS and CVARDD real-world databases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Desmopressin has been associated with hyponatremia-in clinical practice; however, postmarketing real-world evidence on its safety signals, susceptible populations, and time-to-onset (TTO) patterns remains limited. METHODS: This study aimed to characterize desmopressin related adverse event signals in the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS,2004Q1-2025Q4) and the Canadian Vigilance Adverse Reaction Database (CVARDD), focusing on hyponatremia. Signal detection was performed using four disproportionality analysis methods (reporting odds ratio, proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker), with concurrent positivity across all four methods required for signal confirmation. Subgroup analyses were conducted by age and sex. For cases with complete dates, TTO was calculated and modeled using the Weibull distribution. RESULTS: Among 19,906,480 deduplicated reports, 3,878 listed desmopressin as the primary suspect drug. The strongest signals were observed for metabolism and nutrition disorders, particularly hyponatremia-related events (e.g., Hyponatraemia, Blood sodium decreased, Water intoxication, Hyponatraemic encephalopathy), often accompanied by seizures and other serious neurologic events. Age was the main source of heterogeneity: hyponatremia-related RORs were markedly higher in patients aged ≥ 60 years. TTO analysis showed an early-failure pattern, with ~ 60% of AEs occurring within 30 days; the Weibull shape parameter β = 0.36 (95% CI 0.35-0.37) indicated a decreasing hazard over time. Hyponatremia also occurred predominantly early but remained detectable during long-term treatment (≥ 360 days). CONCLUSION: Hyponatremia-related events represented prominent reporting signals for desmopressin in spontaneous-report databases. Cross-database assessment, subgroup heterogeneity, and TTO patterns provide pharmacovigilance context for this established safety concern. These findings characterize reporting patterns and do not quantify clinical incidence or establish causality. They support continued adherence to existing recommendations for patient selection and sodium monitoring during desmopressin therapy.

articles.title: The positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062, attenuates alcohol self-administration in female Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Four-day intragastric treatment with the positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062 (1, 3, and 10 mg/kg), suppressed operant oral alcohol self-administration in male and female Sprague Dawley (SD) rats (Haile et al., Psychopharmacology 238:2587-2600, 2021). Conversely, in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 6-week treatment with ASP8062 (25 mg/day, corresponding to the 3-mg/kg rat dose) failed to attenuate alcohol craving and consumption in individuals with moderate or severe alcohol use disorder (AUD) (Schacht et al., Alcohol Clin Exp Res 48:2352-2363, 2024). Reverse-translational dose-ranging studies in animal models of AUD were suggested. OBJECTIVES: In keeping with this purpose, the present study tested ASP8062 on operant oral alcohol self-administration in selectively bred Sardinian alcohol-preferring (sP) rats, a validated animal model of AUD. METHODS: Female sP rats were trained to lever-respond for alcohol under the fixed ratio 5 schedule of reinforcement. Once lever-responding for alcohol was high and steady, rats underwent a 4-day intragastric treatment with ASP8062 (3, 10, and 17 mg/kg). RESULTS: Only the 17-mg/kg dose reduced, by approximately 40%, lever-responding for alcohol and estimated amount of self-administered alcohol. No dose of ASP8062 altered motor-coordination, as indicated by the results of a concurrent inverted-screen test. CONCLUSIONS: ASP8062 in sP rats was remarkably less potent compared to previous observations in SD rats, suggesting that higher doses of ASP8062 may be needed in rats modeling AUD. If ideally transposed to humans, these data suggest that future clinical studies should consider testing higher doses of ASP8062 before reaching definitive conclusions on its therapeutic potential.
